question: In all of the following enzyme deficiencies, hyperammonemia is a common feature, EXCEPT:

CHAIN: "Carbamoyl Phosphate synthetase (CPS-I) deficiency" -> "urea cycle disruption" -> "accumulation of ammonia" -> "hyperammonemia" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Ornithine transcarbamoylase (OTC) deficiency" -> "urea cycle disruption" -> "accumulation of ammonia" -> "hyperammonemia" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Ornithine amino transferase deficiency" -> "not directly involved in urea cycle" -> "no significant ammonia accumulation" -> "no hyperammonemia" -> 90%
analysis: The urea cycle is responsible for converting ammonia into urea, which is then excreted from the body. Enzyme deficiencies in the urea cycle lead to the accumulation of ammonia, resulting in hyperammonemia. Argininosuccinate synthetase, carbamoyl phosphate synthetase (CPS-I), and ornithine transcarbamoylase (OTC) are all enzymes directly involved in the urea cycle. Deficiencies in these enzymes disrupt the cycle and cause hyperammonemia. Ornithine amino transferase, however, is not part of the urea cycle. Its deficiency does not typically lead to hyperammonemia, as it is involved in a different metabolic pathway. Therefore, the exception where hyperammonemia is not a common feature is ornithine amino transferase deficiency.
